newsitem.title: UK: ITT, Siemens/Racal consortia win UK deal.
newsitem.headline: ITT, Siemens/Racal consortia win UK deal.

text.p: The government said on Thursday that it had decided to ask two consortia which had bid for a defence contract to produce a combat radio system worth more than one billion stg to cooperate on the scheme.
The consortia which had been bidding for the BOWMAN contract are Crossbow led by ITT Corp's UK unit and Yeoman led by Siemens Plessey Systems and Racal Electronics Plc.

"We have decided to issue a request for proposals for initial production and support to Archer, a joint venture company which is being formed by the leaders of Crossbow and Yeoman," defence procurement minister James Arbuthnot said in a written parliamentary answer.
He said the ministry planned to award a contract in 1999 to meet an in-service date of 2002.
The two groups announced last December that they had decided to cut losses and drop their rivalry after competing for the long-delayed order for over five years.
Instead, ITT and Racal said the two groups were proposing to the Ministry of Defence that they should combine their technical, production and manufacturing resources for Bowman.
Racal had said the new alliance could yield joint savings of 100 million pounds in development costs.
With further delays threatened, Racal said both sides' bid costs were in danger of running to 100 million stg apiece on research and development costs.
